title: Healthcare
levelNote: Six tiers in one file. A lesson takes the slice at or below the learner's level, so a beginner meets doctor and nurse and an advanced learner meets triage and consent — same topic, same file, different depth.
goal: Say what hurts, understand what you are told to do, and hold your own in a consulting room.
goal_pt: Dizer o que está doendo, entender o que mandam você fazer, e se virar sozinho num consultório.

I am sorry. What is wrong?

Thank you very much.

lines.text: Good afternoon. I would like an appointment, please.
Of course. Can you tell me your symptoms?
I have a fever and a bad cough.
How long have you had them?
Since Tuesday. It is getting worse.
We have four o'clock today. You should come in.
Four is perfect. Thank you.
Your results were sent over this morning.
And what do they show?
Nothing serious, but we would like to operate next month.
Are there any side effects I should know about?
Some discomfort for a week. Recovery takes about six weeks.
Could you talk me through the risks before I sign anything?
That is exactly what the consent form is for. Let's go through it together.

reading.title: The waiting room
reading.text:
The waiting room is quiet. Six people are sitting on blue chairs. A nurse comes to the door and says a name. A man stands up slowly and follows her.

A small girl is next to her mother. She has a cough. Her mother reads her a book. The girl is not afraid now.

At four o'clock the doctor calls her name. "Your turn," says her mother, and they walk in together.

questions.q: What is wrong with the girl?
Why is the girl not afraid?

reading.title: Two weeks of waiting
reading.text:
Ana had had the pain for a month before she finally called the surgery. The receptionist offered her an appointment on Thursday, and she took it, although she had told herself for weeks that it was nothing.

The doctor listened, asked how long it had been going on, and wrote a referral to a specialist. "It is almost certainly nothing serious," he said, "but I would rather be sure than sorry."

The diagnosis took two more weeks. In that time Ana learned the difference between waiting for bad news and waiting for news, which are not the same thing at all. When the letter came, the treatment it described was shorter than the wait had been.

questions.q: How long had Ana had the pain before calling?
What does the last sentence say about the treatment?
options: It was shorter than the wait

reading.title: Who is seen first
reading.text:
Triage is the least popular idea in any emergency department, and the only one that works. It means that the order in which people are seen has nothing to do with the order in which they arrived, and everything to do with how quickly they will deteriorate if nobody looks at them.

This is difficult to accept when you have been sitting for four hours with a broken wrist, watching people who came in after you disappear through the doors. It feels like unfairness. It is the opposite: it is the department refusing to let arrival time decide who survives the night.

Staff are trained to explain this, and mostly they do, though rarely at the moment you most want to hear it. The wrist will be seen. It will simply be seen after the chest pain, and after the child who has stopped talking, and that ordering is not an accident or an oversight but the whole design.

questions.q: What decides the order in triage?
What does the writer say the four-hour wait feels like?
What is the writer's overall view of triage?
options: It should be replaced by queuing

speaking.tip: Two beats, both short. Do not stretch sick.
HOS-pi-tal. The stress is on the first part.
Headache is HED-ake. The ea is short, like bed.

speaking.text: I need to see a doctor.
You should take this twice a day.
speaking.tip: The l in should is silent. Say shood.
a-POINT-ment. Four syllables, stress in the middle.

speaking.text: How long have you had this pain?
speaking.tip: Have you sounds like hav-yuh in normal speech.

speaking.text: I need a referral to a specialist.

speaking.tip: Side effects is one unit. Do not pause between them.

speaking.text: The results were sent to your doctor.
speaking.tip: re-SULTS. The stress is on the second half.

speaking.text: Could you talk me through the risks?
speaking.tip: Could you often becomes cudja in fast speech.

speaking.text: I would like a second opinion.
speaking.tip: I would like contracts to I'd like. Practise both.
